title: KV policy simulator + adaptive TTL heuristics and automated rollback playbook
creator: Maya Gupta
description: Build a reproducible offline simulator and a small online canary system to recommend KV/prefix cache key shaping and TTL policies that minimize token-cost while meeting latency SLOs. Deliverables: 1) a simulator that consumes historical request traces + prefix-key templates and emits hit-rate, traffic, and cost projections under randomized TTL and key-normalization strategies; 2) an adaptive TTL heuristic module that suggests per-prefix TTL or tiered caching policies (hot/warm/cold) with safety bounds; 3) safe apply pattern: staged canaries, automatic rollback triggers, and an instrumentation checklist integrated into Redwood Console. The goal is to automate low-risk config changes that reduce host-token cost by 10-30% for cacheable workloads while keeping 99th-percentile latency regression under 5%.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator runs end-to-end on a week of production traces and produces hit-rate vs TTL curves per prefix
Adaptive TTL module produces deterministic suggestions for >80% of high-volume prefixes and exposes confidence scores
Console shows cost delta and expected latency impact for proposed policy changes
Canary rollout implemented: 3% -> 10% -> 50% with automated metric checks and rollback on anomaly
Automated rollback triggers on either: +5% tail latency, +10% error rate, or +15% cost deviation from projection
A merging PR with tests and a demo script is approved by runtime and platform eng reviewers
approach_notes: Simulator inputs: sampled request traces (tokenized lengths, model, route), existing KV key patterns, prefix metadata, current TTLs, and observed KV hit events
Model: hybrid analytical + Monte Carlo engine. Analytical for expected steady-state hit-rate for static key distributions; Monte Carlo to capture burstiness and prefix correlation
Key shaping experiments: normalize trailing punctuation, collapse conversation-level context windows into a single prefix, and test hashed-bucket variants to reduce cardinality
TTL policy space: fixed TTLs, exponential backoff TTLs per-key-frequency quartile, and adaptive TTLs driven by recent hit-rate decay metrics
Safety: always run suggested policies in read-only simulation before proposing writes; use canary percentages and time windows to limit blast radius
Rollback: integrate anomaly detector with Console alerts and an infra-runbook that can auto-create a revert PR or invoke runtime-switchover to previous policy snapshot

updates: 2025-03-11: Kickoff with runtime and product. Agreed on primary metric: cost-per-1M-tokens for cacheable routes and 99p latency bound. Assigned trace extraction to ENG infra.

2025-03-12: Early prototype using sampled traces from 2025-02-20 produced expected hit-rate curve for a single high-volume prefix. Observed that naive TTL increase for that prefix reduces token cost by ~22% but increases 99p latency by 2.8% in simulation — acceptable under thresholds.

2025-03-14: Design review with observability team. Decided to expose confidence bands in Console for each suggestion and to require two metrics to pass before auto-apply (sim projection alignment + live canary stability).

2025-03-16: Implemented Monte Carlo module for burst modelling. Found correlation between session-level keys and decreased marginal hit-rate at longer TTLs. This informed a tiered TTL approach (session-prefixed keys short TTL, global prefixes longer TTL).

2025-03-17: Simulator v0 completed. Pushed prototype code: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4821 (link placeholder). Added notebook with per-prefix plots and cost estimates in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1a2bExample

2025-03-18: Started work on canary automation. Implementation plan: feature-flagged policy objects, canary percentages controlled by rollout service, and a metrics-check lambda that compares canary vs baseline. Draft runbook created in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Cache+Sim+Runbook
